short: A Swedish column captured Prague Castle and looted its priceless collections just before the war ended.
full:
In the final months of the Thirty Years' War, a flying Swedish column under Hans Christoff von Königsmarck executed a surprise attack on Prague on 25 July 1648. Aided by a defecting Imperial officer, they rapidly seized Malá Strana (the Lesser Town) and Prague Castle, but were unable to cross the Charles Bridge to take the Old Town on the eastern bank.

For the next three months, the Swedes besieged the Old Town, which was fiercely defended by its citizens and a small garrison. Meanwhile, the Swedes systematically looted the castle's immense treasures, including the famed collections of Emperor Rudolf II, shipping them back to Stockholm. The fighting only ceased when news of the Peace of Westphalia finally reached the city in November.
